description: Canonical payer registry — maps free-text insurance strings (as extracted from clinical notes) to a stable payer_id used to key prior_auth_required / eligibility checks. Aliases are matched case-insensitively as substrings against the note's insurance field; when multiple payers' aliases match, the LONGEST matching alias wins (most specific), so 'humana medicare advantage' resolves to the Medicare Advantage entry, never bare Medicare.

field_notes.kind: medicare_ffs | medicare_advantage | commercial | medicaid | tricare | workers_comp — machine-readable payer class for rule routing.
field_notes.is_medicare: TRUE ONLY for Original (fee-for-service) Medicare. Medicare Advantage is deliberately false — MA plans have their own prior-auth, claims routing, and contractor rules; applying FFS-specific logic to them was a real misclassification bug.
field_notes.follows_medicare_coverage: True where the payer is bound to Original Medicare's coverage floor (FFS itself, and MA plans per 42 CFR 422.101). Coverage-derived checks (LCD medical necessity, routine-foot-care class findings, not-valid-for-Medicare status codes) key off this, NOT is_medicare.

stedi_trading_partner_note: stedi_trading_partner_id is a DIFFERENT namespace from payer_id — it's Stedi's own primaryPayerId, required as tradingPartnerServiceId in eligibility (270/271) API calls. Resolved live via GET https://payers.us.stedi.com/2024-04-01/payers/search?query=<name> (top match), retrieved 2026-07-10. Tricare is region-split by Stedi (East=99727, West=99726) with no single ID for 'Tricare' generically — West was chosen because the prior-auth source document (prior_auth_tricare.json) is from TriWest Healthcare Alliance, the West-region administrator. Verify this matches the practice's actual TRICARE region before relying on it for real eligibility checks. Entries without a stedi_trading_partner_id have not been resolved yet — eligibility checks are skipped for them.

payers.stedi_note: MA claims/eligibility go to the specific plan (Humana, UHC, Aetna...), not CMS — resolve the plan's own Stedi ID before running eligibility. Listed generically here so MA is at least classified correctly instead of falling through to FFS Medicare.

payers.stedi_note: Centene's Florida Medicaid managed-care plan (Statewide Medicaid Managed Care). Classified as medicaid so Medicaid-class rules apply instead of the claim falling through as an unknown payer (observed live: 3 corpus notes with 'Sunshine Health (Centene)' resolved to kind=unknown, skipping every payer-keyed check).
State-specific carriers/TPAs — eligibility and fee schedules vary by jurisdiction; classified generically so WC claims are at least not treated as commercial/Medicare.
